proof.claim:
The controller's persisted node liveness must track reality, no matter how
its state writes are optimized.

THE INCIDENT (2026-08-16). A routine ai-memory package deploy escalated into
a full cluster outage. Along the way etcd hit its 2 GiB backend quota and
went NOSPACE on 4 of 5 members. Investigating the write volume, an
optimization shipped as cluster-controller@1.2.317: the controller's state
blob was no longer rewritten when nothing "semantic" had changed, where
last_seen, reported_at, capabilities.disk_free_bytes and
last_admission_proof.checked_at were all classified as non-semantic
observation, plus a 5-minute floor bounding how often observation drift alone
could trigger a write.

The classification was correct about WHAT changes and wrong about WHO reads
it. last_seen is not decoration on the state record — it is the liveness
signal. Within minutes of the rollout the persisted values were 254-276s
stale against the 300s floor, and readers judging node liveness from
/globular/clustercontroller/state reported 3 of 5 nodes UNREACHABLE with
CRITICAL findings. Every node agent was healthy, listening on its port, and
serving. The control plane was lying about the cluster, not observing it.

The rollback was itself blocked by the desired-state regression floor and
needed --allow-regression.

WHY IT SHIPPED. Four unit tests covered the change. Every one asserted that
a write was SKIPPED — the optimization worked, and all four were green. Not
one asserted that anything still functioned afterwards. A test that pins a
suppression proves the suppression happens; it can never prove the
suppression was safe. That is the same shape as a check that cannot fail
being indistinguishable from one that passes.

The justification was also wrong on its own numbers: the measured load was
~78 KB x ~4/min = ~30 MB/hour, against a 1h compaction retention, so this
writer's steady-state contribution to the backend is bounded at ~30 MB. It
could not have filled 2 GiB. See etcd-backend-does-not-ratchet for what
actually did.

WHAT THIS SCENARIO PINS. On a healthy, idle cluster — where nothing
"semantic" is changing and a content-hash optimization is therefore at its
most tempting — every node's persisted last_seen must stay fresh. The
scenario deliberately waits through a quiet period, because a quiet cluster
is exactly the condition under which the 1.2.317 dedup suppressed writes.

Failure of this scenario means liveness in etcd has drifted from liveness in
reality, whatever the mechanism.
